summary: Iteration 18 (configurable session_multipliers + differentiated warning_kind badge) verified. Backend: 13/13 pytest passing — POST/PUT /api/teams accept & validate session_multipliers, reject invalid (0, 5, 'foo', -1) with 400; values flow into /api/analytics/athlete session_multiplier and load_adjusted (match=1.5 verified); metrics.warning_kind field present with correct enum values; regression PDFs (athlete full, team full, weekly, monthly) return 200 with %PDF header. Frontend: Team Edit form shows 'Multiplicadores por Tipo de Sessão' block with 4 inputs; editing (match=1.5, training=1.1) persists across reload; 'Repor predefinidos' (mult-reset) restores 1.0/1.2/1.0/0.7; dashboard risk-alert cells display blue 'SUB-TREINO' badges for demo detraining athletes (matches WARNING_KIND_META.detraining #00B0FF).

minor.issue: Unlike PUT, POST silently drops invalid session_multipliers (returns None from _sanitize_multipliers without HTTP 400). Inconsistent with PUT behaviour. Low-severity since UI never posts invalid values and the request just falls back to defaults.

action_items: Optional: make POST /api/teams reject invalid session_multipliers with 400 for parity with PUT.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to 4389 lines — consider splitting into routers (teams, analytics, exports, seed) for maintainability.
_sanitize_multipliers used inconsistently: POST silently discards invalid dict, PUT returns 400. Unify behaviour.
Frontend Bits.jsx / risk badge mapping is fully data-driven via WARNING_KIND_META — clean & extensible.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing demo seed. Restored team session_multipliers back to defaults (1.0/1.2/1.0/0.7) after each mutation test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 18 fully green. Demo seed produces warning_kind='detraining' for most athletes — to exercise other kinds (acwr_alert/monotony/strain/wellness) you'd need to synthesise session data. Backend regression suite for iterations 14-17 still passing via test_iteration18 subset (full PDFs, weekly/monthly PDFs).
